hypothesis: Buying S&P 500 stocks right after a big, fast breakout (5-day gain of at least 8%, a new 20-day closing high, volume at least 1.5x normal) and selling with a 4% stop-loss, an 8% trailing stop, or after 20 days, earns a better risk-adjusted return than SPY after costs.
rationale: Cutting losses quickly while letting winners run should make average wins larger than average losses even with a low win rate. Counter-evidence on this exact data: last week's biggest gainers tended to UNDERPERFORM over the following week and month (5-day return raw IC about -0.016 at 5 days and -0.026 at 21 days). Tight stops on volatile stocks are also often hit by ordinary noise. Tested once, honestly, as the user's idea.
prior_evidence: 5-day winners underperformed afterwards in this universe (raw IC about -0.016 at 5 days, -0.026 at 21 days).

rule.execution: buy at next open; hard stop intraday (gap exits at open); trailing stop and time exit at close

decision_rule: If every gate passes: freeze as qualified and forward-test for 12 months against SPY. If any gate fails: close H5; do not try other gain thresholds, stop distances or holding periods on this data.
